guidelines.detail: same as LRN-031 (The reference models the actor's checking and ordering on the in-stock and not-in-stock outcomes as user tasks placed directly after the gateway. The generated model has tasks on those same outcomes with the same flow structure, but it types them as generic tasks, and the order task carries a different label. The records M1, M2, F10, F11, G5, G6, and X4 show this as a difference in element choice )

same as LRN-050 (In the reference, the two branch activities after the 'in stock' decision check and order the specific item named in that branch. The generated model labels them with a broader noun ('plastic') instead of the item the description names in those branches ('color'), which is the same label-fidelity error that LRN-050 covers for user tasks (use the description's own verb and object, do not substitute)

new guideline (Three reference receive tasks (replies to the sent sketches, the printer's status, and the order confirmation) have no counterpart in the generated model. The generator instead modeled only the sending activities and a receive for the 3D model draft (X2), so the replies were left implicit. The closest documented guidelines (ACT-07, GW-03, GW-06, PROC-04, FLOW-06, GW-04) cover activities, merges an)

refines ACT-07 (The reference models a receive of the returned work after sending the sketches, followed by an acceptance gateway that loops back for changes (M1, and the gateway in the reference is missing). The generated model instead has a receive of a draft (X2) and no acceptance decision or loop, so the structure diverges from the description (S2). The description states the repeated change requests explicit)
kept for this example only, tied to it by: change, result, satisfied, what

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a decision or check leads to a named action on the item (for example a stated approval, a required revision, or a detected high-risk condition), and that the action is followed by further steps before the process continues: Model the named action as its own task on the sequence flow of that decision outcome, placed after the gateway and before the next step. Do not connect the decision gateway directly to the following step, and do not fold the action into the gateway label or the next task's label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a decision has an outcome on which the described actor personally performs a work action on the item, such as checking a remaining quantity or ordering something that is missing, and no automated system performs that action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names an action that a participant performs on a business object, using a specific verb (for example 'enter', 'submit', 'rate' or 'negotiate'): Label the corresponding user task with the verb and object the description uses for that action. Do not replace the verb with a synonym or a broader verb that changes what the action means, and do not add a state or outcome the description does not state.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a decision branch checks or orders an item and names that item with a specific noun, and a broader or different noun for the same kind of item appears elsewhere in the description

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after you send a request, a set of files, or an order to another party, that party sends something back (a reply, a status, or a confirmation) that the following activities or decisions depend on: Model that returning message as its own receive element placed after the sending activity and before the first activity or decision that uses it. Use a receive task when the receiving is an activity the process performs, and an intermediate message catch event when the process only waits for the message. Do not fold the reply into the sending activity or into the next activity, and do not omit it because the sending activity seems to cover the exchange. When the description says the other party keeps sending updates while you carry on with other work, model the receipt of those updates as a receive element that is attached to or runs alongside the activity that uses them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after you send a request, a set of files, or an order to another party, that party sends something back (a reply, a status, or a confirmation) that the following activities or decisions depend on

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after work is sent to another party, the process repeatedly asks for changes until the work is accepted, so the next activity depends on whether the returned work is accepted: Model the returned work as a receive element placed after the sending activity. Place an exclusive gateway after that receive element with one outgoing flow for 'accepted', which continues the process, and one for 'not accepted', which returns to the activity that requests changes, forming a revision loop. Do not collapse the loop into a linear sequence, and do not leave the acceptance decision implicit.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after work is sent to another party, the process repeatedly asks for changes until the work is accepted, so the next activity depends on whether the returned work is accepted

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the actor sends material or a draft to an outside party and then repeatedly tells that party what to change until the actor is satisfied with the returned result: Model the returned revised result as its own receive element placed after the sending activity and before the decision that checks satisfaction. Model the feedback to the outside party as a task. Route the decision back to that feedback task when the actor is not satisfied, so the receive element sits inside the loop. Do not model the returned result as part of the sending activity, the feedback task, or the decision.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the actor sends material or a draft to an outside party and then repeatedly tells that party what to change until the actor is satisfied with the returned result
